execution.raw_traces: climate-null/*_trace.json; four chains, each 199 sampled matrices

design.primary_endpoint: B: introduced host incidences in butterfly resource regions already covered by at least one native known host
design.constraints: Butterfly-host identities and all native host ranges fixed. Introduced host-region double-edge switches preserve plant-family richness per region and each plant's number of introduced regions within continent and regional BIO1/BIO12 quantile stratum.
design.quantile_bins: Within each WGSRPD1 continent, classify regional BIO1 and BIO12 independently into two or three quantile bins. Equal values are not split. Missing-climate regions are uniquely frozen in every new model.
design.not_used_for_stratification: Butterfly presence, fitted niche-mismatch, occurrence effort, or observed ecological response
design.sample_consistency_warning: Resolved host species >= recorded host families is a minimum taxonomy consistency criterion, not proof of complete host-use records.

accounting.identity: T = B + D + U; holds per butterfly and for every randomized panel
accounting.T: introduced known-host x butterfly x WGSRPD3 incidences
accounting.B: introduced incidences in regions already covered by at least one native known host
accounting.D: extra introduced-host incidences beyond the first in each new region outside the native resource envelope
accounting.U: unique newly added butterfly x WGSRPD3 resource cells
accounting.interpretation: These are static regional range incidences, not observed local resource use or historical arrival events.

interpretation.residual_effect_size: Primary B excess is 366.49 / 73,748 incidences = about 0.497 percentage points. It is statistically resolved within this constrained null but small in absolute incidence share.
interpretation.added_geography: In the primary 191-species panel, U=13,529 vs climate-null mean 13,823.19: about 2.13% fewer new resource cells than expected, compared with 6.36% under the no-climate benchmark.
interpretation.single_host_redundancy: No positive excess of pooled single-host new-resource share was detected in either climate resolution or the independent-seed sensitivity. This is not evidence of an exact zero effect.
interpretation.headline: Coarse climate conditioning strongly attenuates, but does not eliminate, the excess alignment of introduced known hosts with butterflies' pre-existing native-host resource geography.

independent_validation.method: Independently read accepted interactions and native/contemporary distributions and reconstructed T/B/D/U with SciPy integer sparse matrix products, without importing the geographic-null engine.
independent_validation.trace_checks: Recomputed all model/panel mean, 2.5-97.5 percentile and upper/lower +1 Monte Carlo p values; checked T=B+D+U in every panel-replicate.

test_evidence.original_execution_actual: 86 passed, 1 failed, 1 skipped; the failing test was tests/test_repository_layout.py::test_active_protocol_and_result_surfaces_are_whitelisted. The original workflow piped pytest to tee and incorrectly reported success. Do not cite its success badge as all-suite success.
test_evidence.repair: Moved three dated post-hoc notes from docs/exploratory into provenance/reviewer_defenses/notes without weakening the active-protocol whitelist. Added an explicit-Bash/pipefail verification workflow, installed optional review dependencies, and fixed the climate workflow's pipeline and fail-fast behavior.

limits: Post-hoc same-data analysis. Regional BIO1/BIO12 medians and quantile bins do not control seasonality, within-region climate variation, fine geographic contiguity, human introduction routes or recording effort. Attenuation is not a causal climate-effect percentage. No demographic benefit, local larval use, adaptation or colonization timing is demonstrated. Samples are from constrained swap chains; p resolution is 0.005 per chain, AR1 ESS is approximate, and numerical replication is not independent biological validation.
